title: Prevalence of sarcopenia among community-dwelling older adults in an urban district in Penang, Malaysia and its associated factors
content:
by Sing Wei Low, Zhi Huang See, Norshahida Abdul Hamid, Winnie Ker Chien Oung, Yusnita Yusof, Ying Woei Chin, Azianey Yusof Abdullah Saari

Background

Sarcopenia refers to a progressive decline in skeletal muscle mass, strength, and physical performance that commonly occurs with ageing, and is associated with adverse outcomes such as frailty, disability, and mortality. Despite its growing public health importance in ageing populations, limited data are available on the prevalence of sarcopenia in Penang, Malaysia. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of sarcopenia and its associated factors among community-dwelling older adults in an urban district in Penang.

Methods

A cross-sectional study was conducted among community-dwelling adults aged 60 years and above in the Seberang Perai Utara district, Penang. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling. Sarcopenia was diagnosed using the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) 2019 criteria based on muscle mass, muscle strength, and physical performance. Data on sociodemographic characteristics, comorbidities, and physical activity levels were collected using a structured questionnaire and the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ) short form. Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with sarcopenia.

Results

A total of 226 participants were included in the study. The overall prevalence of sarcopenia was 32.7%, including 15.0% with severe sarcopenia and 17.7% with sarcopenia. In multivariate analysis, higher body mass index (adjusted OR 0.794, 95% CI 0.723–0.873, p < 0.001) was associated with lower odds of sarcopenia. Physical activity level was also significantly associated with sarcopenia (p = 0.013). Participants who were minimally active had higher odds of sarcopenia (adjusted OR = 4.393, 95% CI: 1.583–12.193, p = 0.004) compared with HEPA active participants.

Conclusion

Sarcopenia was identified in nearly one-third of participants among community-dwelling older adults in Seberang Perai Utara, Penang. Compared with HEPA active participants, minimally active participants were associated with higher odds of sarcopenia. Whereas higher BMI was associated with lower odds of the condition. These findings highlight key cross-sectional correlates of sarcopenia in community, emphasizing the importance of monitoring body weight, muscle health, and physical activity engagement among community-dwelling older adults.
